title: Spectral Progressive Diffusion for Efficient Image and Video Generation
claim: Growing resolution progressively along the denoising trajectory, with noise re-injected at each transition, avoids wasted high-resolution compute on noise-dominated frequencies.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, timeline with zoom-in callout to detail box
description: A wide figure in two parts. On the left, a horizontal timeline runs from t=1 to t=0 with colored dots at t1, t2 and t3. Colored bars below it mark resolution stages s1=0.25, s2=0.5, s3=0.75 and s4=1, in blue, orange, green and red. Under the bars, a row of corgi images goes from noisy and small to sharp and full-size, with each image's size matching its stage. A log-scale power spectrum plot P(ω) ∝ ω^-β sits at the bottom left. Its curve uses the same stage colors, and it is labeled 'Optimal resolution schedule'. A black box highlights one transition, and an arrow leads from it to a cream-colored panel on the right. That panel is titled 'Spectral noise expansion'. It shows a low-resolution noisy image going through a transform T_Φ into a Fourier-domain image padded with noise ε, then through T_Φ^-1 to a higher-resolution image.
caption: Spectral Progressive Diffusion. We progressively grow the resolution along the denoising trajectory using an optimal resolution schedule derived from the spectral power of pretrained models (left). At each scheduled transition, our spectral noise expansion mechanism (right) injects high-frequency noise at the correct level while preserving the partially-denoised low-frequency content.
abstract: Diffusion models have been shown to implicitly generate visual content autoregressively in the frequency domain, where low-frequency components are generated earlier in the denoising process while high-frequency details emerge only in later timesteps. This structure offers a natural opportunity for efficient generation, as high-resolution computation on noise-dominated frequencies is largely redundant. We propose Spectral Progressive Diffusion, a general framework that progressively grows resolution along the denoising trajectory of pretrained diffusion models. To this end, we develop a spectral noise expansion mechanism and derive an optimal resolution schedule from the model's power spectrum. Our framework supports training-free acceleration and a novel fine-tuning recipe that further improves efficiency and quality. We demonstrate significant speedups on state-of-the-art pretrained image and video generation models while preserving visual quality.
